intro: Scarborough is where a lot of Toronto actually eats: Hakka and Cantonese in Agincourt, Sri Lankan and South Indian along Lawrence and Markham Road, Caribbean all over. It's spread out and unglamorous, and that's the point — these are the places people drive across the city for.

picks.name: Federick Restaurant
picks.why: A Scarborough Hakka institution — Indian-Chinese chilli chicken, Manchurian and hot garlic dishes that many locals swear by.

picks.name: Fishman Lobster Clubhouse Restaurant
picks.why: Famous for towering platters of lobster fried with ginger and scallion. Come with a group and plan to share.

picks.name: Johnny's Hamburgers
picks.why: Old-school burger stand that's been flipping charbroiled burgers for decades. No frills, very satisfying.

picks.name: Babu Catering
picks.why: Sri Lankan Tamil cooking — kothu roti, string hoppers and fiery curries — the kind of place Scarborough's Sri Lankan community has relied on for years.

picks.name: Saravanaa Bhavan
picks.why: South Indian vegetarian classics — giant dosas, idli and thalis — from a well-known Chennai-born chain.

picks.name: Scotty Bons
picks.why: Jamaican and Caribbean comfort food — jerk chicken, oxtail and rice and peas in generous portions.

picks.name: Congee Queen
picks.why: Cantonese comfort food with a huge menu — congee, noodles, and plenty to share when nobody can agree.
